Multi-scale Gaussian process spatial structure

Source: R/spatial_gp.R
spatial_multiscale.Rd

Specify a multi-scale spatial random effect that decomposes spatial variation into local (fine-scale) and regional (broad-scale) components. Each scale has its own range and variance parameters.

Usage

spatial_multiscale(
  coords,
  scales = c("local", "regional"),
  approx = c("nngp", "hsgp"),
  m = NULL,
  c_boundary = NULL,
  range_local = NULL,
  range_regional = c(1, 10),
  cov = NULL,
  nu = 1.5,
  nn_local = 10,
  nn_regional = 30,
  shared = NULL,
  scale_coords = TRUE,
  sampler = c("auto", "noncentered", "centered")
)

# S3 method for class 'tulpa_multiscale'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

coords

A one-sided formula specifying coordinate columns (e.g., ~ lon + lat), or a character vector of length 2 with column names.

scales

Character vector specifying scale names. Default: c("local", "regional").

approx

Approximation method: "nngp" (default) for Nearest Neighbor GP; "hsgp" for a Hilbert-space basis shared by both scales, which is fitted by the nested-Laplace path only (mode = "auto" or "nested_laplace"); the samplers carry the NNGP form.

m

Number of HSGP basis functions per dimension, between 3 and 50; only used when approx = "hsgp", where each scale carries its own basis of m^2 functions. A value given applies to both scales. NULL (default) chooses each scale's from the data by the rule spatial_gp() describes: first at the median of that scale's range prior, then at its posterior median lengthscale while the basis does not represent it.

c_boundary

Boundary factor for HSGP domain extension, >= 1; only used when approx = "hsgp". A value given applies to both scales; NULL (default) chooses each scale's from the data.

range_local

Plausible range interval for the local scale as c(lower, upper) in coordinate units. NULL (default) takes the upper bound 1 (after scaling) and the lower bound from the data: the median, over the distinct locations, of the distance to the nearest other location. A range below the spacing of the locations is one the data do not inform, and with approx = "hsgp" a lower bound there asks the basis rule for more functions than the data can use. This is not a hard box: lower anchors a PC prior on that scale's range (P(range < lower) = 0.05, the same prior spatial_gp() uses), on every route that fits the field; a sampler starts the range at the pair's geometric mean. The range itself is free on (0, Inf). The range is the Matern range rho = 2 * ell, matching spatial_spde(), on both approximations. Here ell is the kernel lengthscale (phi in the NNGP kernels). The squared-exponential kernel uses the same effective-range convention.

range_regional

Plausible range interval for the regional scale, read the same way. Default: c(1, 10) (after scaling). Keeping the two intervals separated is what identifies the scales against each other.

cov

Covariance function, read as spatial_gp() reads it: with approx = "nngp", "exponential" (default) or "matern"; with approx = "hsgp", "matern" (default, at nu = 1.5) or "squared_exponential".

nu

Smoothness parameter for Matern covariance, one of 1.5 or 2.5.

nn_local

Number of nearest neighbors for local scale. Default 10.

nn_regional

Number of nearest neighbors for regional scale. Default 30.

shared

Logical; if TRUE (default), spatial effects enter both all processes.

scale_coords

Logical; if TRUE (default), coordinates are centred and divided by one common factor before computing distances (see spatial_gp()).

sampler

Latent parameterization for the exact-NUTS field. "auto" (default) and "noncentered" sample z ~ N(0, I) per scale and reconstruct each field as w = f(z, sigma2, phi), avoiding the field/hyperparameter funnel; "centered" places the NNGP density on each field directly.

x

A tulpa_multiscale specification.

...

Ignored.

Value

A tulpa_multiscale object

Details

The multi-scale model decomposes spatial variation additively:

$$\eta(s) = X\beta + w_{local}(s) + w_{regional}(s)$$

where each component follows an independent Gaussian process: $$w_{local}(s) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2_{local} C(\phi_{local}))$$ $$w_{regional}(s) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2_{regional} C(\phi_{regional}))$$

Fitting. mode = "auto", "structured" and "nested_laplace" fit the field by nested Laplace, as two field blocks of the multi-block driver (two NNGP blocks, each on its own neighbour structure, or two HSGP blocks on one basis). Each scale carries its own SD and range axes on the outer grid, placed and refined like any other field axis, so both scales' variances and ranges are integrated. The exact samplers (mode = "exact" and its siblings) sample the NNGP form with the same priors. spatial_range() reports each scale's sigma and range (3 * phi), tagged [local] / [regional]; field_effects() reports the summed field per distinct location, or one scale with component =.

Identifiability. Both fields are proper, so neither needs a level constraint; the constant they share with the intercept is held by their priors. What tells the scales apart is the range priors: the regional field's PC prior puts 5% of its mass below range_regional[1], and the local field's below range_local[1], while neither range is bounded above. Where the data do not separate the scales, the local range can therefore reach into the regional interval and the two scales share the variance, which widens both intervals rather than switching the labels. On simulated Poisson data with 300 locations on a 10 x 10 square (local SD 0.63 and range 0.5, regional SD 1 and range 3, range_local = c(0.2, 1.5), range_regional = c(1.5, 10)), the nested 95% intervals of all four hyperparameters covered the truth on each of 5 data sets, with posterior means 0.66 / 1.1 (local SD / range) and 1.03 / 7.3 (regional); the component maps correlated with the simulated fields at 0.49 (local), 0.79 (regional) and 0.85 (sum).

Computational cost. On those data sets the nested fit took 97-125 s (100 locations: 29 s). Exact NUTS on 100 locations took 453 s for 4 chains of 1000 iterations and had not converged (R-hat 1.14 and bulk ESS 13 on the local log-variance), its chains disagreeing on how the variance splits between the scales.

See also

spatial_gp() for single-scale GP, temporal_multiscale() for multi-scale temporal effects

Examples

# Create multi-scale spatial structure
ms <- spatial_multiscale(
  ~ lon + lat,
  range_local = c(0.1, 0.5),
  range_regional = c(1, 5)
)
print(ms)
#> tulpa Multi-Scale spatial specification
#> ========================================
#> 
#> Coordinates: lon, lat 
#> Scales: local + regional 
#> 
#> Local scale:
#>   Range prior: [0.1, 0.5]
#>   Neighbors: 10 
#> 
#> Regional scale:
#>   Range prior: [1, 5]
#>   Neighbors: 30 
#> 
#> Covariance: exponential 
#> Shared: Yes (enters both processes) 

# \donttest{
set.seed(101)
n <- 25
df <- data.frame(
  lon = runif(n, 0, 10),
  lat = runif(n, 0, 10),
  depth = rnorm(n),
  temp = rnorm(n)
)
df$count <- rpois(n, exp(1 + 0.2 * df$depth))

# Both scales' variances and ranges are integrated by nested Laplace.
fit <- tulpa(
  count ~ depth + temp,
  data = df,
  family = "poisson",
  spatial = spatial_multiscale(
    ~ lon + lat,
    range_local = c(0.1, 0.5),
    range_regional = c(1, 5),
    nn_local = 5L,
    nn_regional = 8L
  )
)
#> [nested-laplace] preparing joint Hessian sparsity pattern
#> [nested-laplace] 1/625 cells (0%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=1s | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 191/191 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] preparing joint Hessian sparsity pattern
#> [nested-laplace] 1/625 cells (0%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=1s | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 275/275 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells
spatial_range(fit)
#>                      mean        sd       q2.5       q97.5
#> sigma[local]    0.2588812 0.2016770 0.01019120   0.7182364
#> range[local]          Inf       Inf 0.35671721  77.2081895
#> sigma[regional] 0.3550972 0.3128667 0.01230064   1.1595261
#> range[regional]       Inf       Inf 3.63862499 688.0435731
head(field_effects(fit, component = "regional"))
